titulo: Unfair or unauthorized billing on credit cards or consumer loans

fundamentos_legais.texto_resumido: Unfair or deceptive acts or practices in commerce are unlawful, including billing consumers for amounts not owed.
Creditors must disclose credit terms and provide billing error rights, including procedures to dispute unauthorized charges.
Within five days of initial communication, a debt collector must send validation information and cease collection if the debt is disputed until verification is provided.

jurisprudencia.numero_processo: FTC v. Credit Bureau Center, LLC (7th Cir.)
jurisprudencia.resultado_resumido: Federal consumer protection statutes apply to credit reporting and billing practices by financial institutions and their vendors.

jurisprudencia.numero_processo: CFPB v. Wells Fargo (2022 consent order)
jurisprudencia.resultado_resumido: Unfair billing and unauthorized fees may require restitution and corrective action when the creditor cannot show a good-faith error.
Order dated 2025-08-06. Credit card billing error. No good-faith error shown; restitution ordered; emotional distress damages denied on these facts.
Order dated 2025-06-25. Credit card billing error. Good-faith error recognized; simple refund only (not double restitution); emotional distress damages denied.
